newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen weaker on brokerage worries.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen weaker on brokerage worries.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to extend their losses on Thursday due to growing worries over wider effects of a corporate racketeer scandal involving Nomura Securities, brokers said. Concern grew after Tokyo prosecutors raided Yamaichi Securities on Wednesday.
But they said major blue-chip issues are expected to gain ground, backed by the yen's weakness and U.S. stocks' rally, helping to limit any falls in the key stock index.
On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished 189.92 points or 0.93 percent lower at 20,212.82. Its September futures closed down 180 points at 20,220.

"The Nikkei 225 is not likely to post a rebound easily," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house. "I suppose many people want to see what would happen next to other major securities houses after the raid on Yamaichi."

Brokers also said worries over construction firms' financial health may weigh on their share prices, following the news late on Wednesday that Tada Corp had applied for court protection under Japanese bankruptcy laws.
But major exporters in the high-tech sector are expected to remain solid, although they may see some profit-taking, and this will help underpin the overall market, they said.
